children.text: citro ha vai gārgyāyaṇir yakṣyamāṇa āruṇiṃ vavre
children.translated_text: <s>Citra Gārgyāyaṇi</s>, being about to sacrifice, chose <s>Āruṇi</s>.

children.text: sa ha putraṃ śvetaketuṃ prajighāya yājayeti
children.translated_text: He sent his son <s>Śvetaketu</s>, saying, "Perform the sacrifice."
When he was seated, he asked him:

children.text: gautamasya putrāsti saṃvṛtaṃ loke yasmin mā dhāsyasyanyatamo vādhvā tasya
children.translated_text: "Son of <s>Gautama</s>, is there a hidden place in the world in which you will place me, or is there some other path of his
by which you will place me in the world?"
He said, "I do not know this."
"Well then, I shall ask the teacher."

children.text: sa ha pitaram āsādya papracchetīti māprākṣīt kathaṃ pratibravāṇīti
children.translated_text: He went to his father and asked, "Thus he questioned me; how should I answer?"
He said, "I too do not know this.

children.text: sadasyeva vayaṃ svādhyāyam adhītya harāmahe yan naḥ pare dadati
children.translated_text: We have merely studied the recitation in the assembly and carried away what others gave us.
Come, we two shall go."
So, with fuel in hand, he approached <s>Citra Gārgyāyaṇi</s>.
"May I come near?" he said to him.

children.text: brahmārgho 'si gautama yo na mānam upāgāḥ
children.translated_text: "You are worthy of the brahman-offering, <s>Gautama</s>, since you have come without pride.
Come; indeed I shall make you understand."

children.text: sa hovāca ye vai ke cāsmāllokāt prayanti candramasam eva te sarve gacchanti
children.translated_text: He said: "Whoever depart from this world all go to the moon.
By their breaths the bright fortnight is filled up.
By the dark fortnight it sends them forth again.
The moon is indeed the gate of the heavenly world.
Whoever answers it, it lets pass beyond.

children.text: atha ya enam na pratyāha tam iha vṛṣṭirbhūtvā varṣati
children.translated_text: But whoever does not answer it, him it rains down here as rain.

children.text: sa iha kīṭo vā pataṅgo vā matsyo vā śakunir vā siṃho vā varāho vā parasvān vā śārdūlo vā puruṣo vānyo vā teṣu teṣu sthāneṣu pratyājāyate yathākarma yathāvidyam
children.translated_text: Here he is born again in these various stations, according to karma and according to knowledge: as a worm, or a moth, or a fish, or a bird, or a lion, or a boar, or a snake, or a tiger, or a human being, or something else.
It asks him when he has arrived, "Who are you?"

children.text: taṃ pratibrūyād vicakṣaṇād ṛtavo reta ābhṛtaṃ pañcadaśāt prasūtāt pitryāvatas tan mā puṃsi kartaryerayadhvaṃ puṃsā kartrā mātari māsiṣikta
children.translated_text: He should answer it: "From the discerning one the seasons brought the seed, from the fifteenfold one produced, from the world of the fathers. Send that into a male agent; by a male agent pour me into a mother.
Being born and coming to birth, I am the twelfth or thirteenth month.
By the twelfth or thirteenth father

children.text: saṃ tad vide 'haṃ prati tad vide 'haṃ tan ma ṛtavo 'mṛtyava ābharadhvam
children.translated_text: I know that; I know that in return. Seasons, immortal ones, bring that to me.

children.text: tena satyena tena tapasa ṛturasmyārtavo 'smi ko 'smi tvam asmi
children.translated_text: By that truth, by that austerity, I am a season, I am seasonal. Who am I? I am you."
Then it lets him pass beyond.

children.text: sa etaṃ devayānaṃ panthānam āpadyāgnilokam āgacchati
children.translated_text: He enters this <s>devayāna</s> (path of the gods) and reaches the world of fire.
He reaches the world of wind.
He reaches the world of the sun.
He reaches the world of <s>Varuṇa</s>.
He reaches the world of <s>Indra</s>.
He reaches the world of <s>Prajāpati</s>.
He reaches the world of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: tasya ha vā etasya lokasyāro hradaḥ
children.translated_text: Of that world there is the lake <s>Āra</s>.
The moments are the staff-bearers.
There is the river <s>Vijarā</s>.
There is the tree <s>Ilya</s>.
There is the dwelling called <s>Sālajya</s>.
There is the abode called <s>Aparājita</s>.
<s>Indra</s> and <s>Prajāpati</s> are the two doorkeepers.
There is the measured hall <s>Vibhu</s>.
There is the couch <s>Vicakṣaṇā</s>.
There is the bed <s>Amitaujas</s>.
There are <s>Priyā</s>, the mental one,
and <s>Pratirūpā</s>, the visual one.
Taking flowers, they weave the worlds.
There are the apsarases <s>Ambā</s> and <s>Ambāyavī</s>.
The rivers are called <s>Āmbayā</s>.
He comes to the lake <s>Āra</s>.
He crosses it by the mind.
Those who know only the immediate present sink when they reach it.
He comes to the moments, the staff-bearers.
They run away from him.
He comes to the river <s>Vijarā</s>, free from old age.
He crosses it by the mind alone.
There he shakes off good and evil deeds.
His dear kinsmen obtain his good deed.
The undear obtain his evil deed.

children.text: tad yathā rathena dhāvayan rathacakre paryavekṣetaivam ahorātre paryavekṣata evaṃ sukṛtaduṣkṛte sarvāṇi ca dvandvāni
children.translated_text: As one driving in a chariot might look down upon the two wheels of the chariot, so he looks down upon day and night, upon good and evil deeds, and upon all pairs of opposites.

children.text: sa eṣa visukṛto viduṣkṛto brahma vidvān brahmaivābhipraiti
children.translated_text: Thus, rid of good deed and rid of evil deed, knowing <s>Brahman</s>, he goes onward to <s>Brahman</s> itself.
The one who knows thus comes to him.
<s>Brahman</s> says of him, "Run toward him with my glory.
He has reached the river <s>Vijarā</s>.
Indeed he will not grow old."

children.text: taṃ pañcaśatānyapsarasāṃ pratiyanti śataṃ mālyahastāḥ śatam āñjanahastāḥ śataṃ cūrṇahastāḥ śataṃ vāsohastāḥ śataṃ phalahastāḥ
children.translated_text: Five hundred apsarases go toward him: one hundred with garlands in hand, one hundred with collyrium in hand, one hundred with powder in hand, one hundred with garments in hand, and one hundred with fruits in hand.
They adorn him with the adornment of <s>Brahman</s>.
Adorned with the adornment of <s>Brahman</s>, the knower goes onward to <s>Brahman</s>.
He comes to the tree <s>Ilya</s>.
The fragrance of <s>Brahman</s> enters him.
He comes to the dwelling <s>Sālajya</s>.
The savor of <s>Brahman</s> enters him.
He comes to the abode <s>Aparājita</s>.
The splendor of <s>Brahman</s> enters him.
He comes to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Prajāpati</s>, the two doorkeepers.
They both run away from him.
He comes to the measured hall <s>Vibhu</s>.
The fame of <s>Brahman</s> enters him.
He comes to the couch <s>Vicakṣaṇā</s>.
The two sāmans <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> are its front feet.
The <s>Śyaita</s> and <s>Naudhasa</s> are its rear feet.
The <s>Vairūpa</s> and <s>Vairāja</s> are its lengthwise pieces.
The <s>Śākvara</s> and <s>Raivata</s> are its cross-pieces.
That couch is insight.
For by insight one sees clearly.
He comes to the bed <s>Amitaujas</s>.
It is <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath).

children.text: tasya bhūtaṃ ca bhaviṣyacca pūrvau pādau
children.translated_text: Past and future are its front feet.
<s>Śrī</s> and <s>Irā</s> are its rear feet.
The <s>Bhadra</s> and <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s> are the head-pieces.
The ṛcs and sāmans are the lengthwise stretchings.
The yajuses are the crosswise ones.
The soma-stalks are the mattress.
The <s>udgītha</s> (chant) is the support.
<s>Śrī</s> is the pillow.
On it <s>Brahman</s> sits.
The one who knows thus climbs upon it first with one foot only.
<s>Brahman</s> says to him, "Who are you?"
He should answer him:
"I am a season.
I am seasonal.
Born from the womb of space, as seed for radiance,
I am the splendor of the year, the self of every being.
You are the self of every being.
What you are, that am I."
He says to him, "Who am I?"
He should say, "Truth."
"What is that which is truth?"

children.text: yad anyad devebhyaśca prāṇebhyaśca tat sat
children.translated_text: What is other than the gods and the vital powers, that is sat, “being.”

children.text: atha yad devāśca prāṇāśca tat tyaṃ tad ekayā vācābhivyāhriyate sattyam iti
children.translated_text: And what consists of the gods and the vital powers, that is tyam; by one utterance that is expressed as sattyam, “truth.”
This much is all this.
You are all this.
Thus indeed he says this to him.
This has been declared by a verse of the Ṛgveda:
Having the Yajus as belly, the Sāman as head, that imperishable one has the Ṛc as its form.

children.text: sa brahmeti sa vijñeya ṛṣirbrahmamayo mahān
children.translated_text: He is Brahman; he should be known as the great seer made of Brahman.
Thus.
He says to him:
“By what do you obtain my masculine names?”
He should say, “By <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath).”
“By what the neuter names?”
“By the mind.”
“By what the feminine names?”
“By speech.”
“By what smells?”
“By the nose.”
“By what forms?”
“By the eye.”
“By what sounds?”
“By the ear.”
“By what the tastes of food?”
“By the tongue.”
“By what actions?”
“By the two hands.”
“By what pleasure and pain?”
“By the body.”
“By what bliss, delight, and procreation?” “By the generative organ.”
“By what goings?”
“By the two feet.”
“By what are thoughts and desires to be known?”
He should say, “By intelligence alone.”

children.text: tam āha āpo vai khalu me lokam
children.translated_text: He says to him, “The waters indeed are my world.”
“This is that world of yours.”

children.text: sā yā brahmaṇo jitir yā vyaṣṭis tāṃ jitiṃ jayati tāṃ vyaṣṭiṃ vyaśnute ya evaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Whoever knows thus wins that victory which is Brahman’s victory, and attains that expansion which is Brahman’s expansion; whoever knows thus, whoever knows thus.
<s>Prāṇa</s> is Brahman, so <s>Kauṣītaki</s> used to say.

children.text: tasya ha vā etasya prāṇasya brahmaṇo mano dūtam
children.translated_text: Of this <s>prāṇa</s>, this Brahman, the mind is the messenger.
The eye is the protector.
The ear is the announcer.

children.text: vāk pariveṣṭrī sa yo ha vā etasya prāṇasya brahmaṇo mano dūtam veda dūtavān bhavati
children.translated_text: Speech is the attendant. Whoever knows the mind as the messenger of this <s>prāṇa</s>, this Brahman, becomes possessed of a messenger.
Whoever knows the eye as protector becomes possessed of a protector.
Whoever knows the ear as announcer becomes possessed of an announcer.

children.text: yo vācaṃ pariveṣṭrīm pariveṣṭrīmān bhavati tasmai vā etasmai prāṇāya brahmaṇa etāḥ sarvā devatā ayācamānāya baliṃ haranti
children.translated_text: Whoever knows speech as attendant becomes possessed of an attendant. To this <s>prāṇa</s>, this Brahman, all these deities bring tribute unasked.

children.text: evaṃ haivāsmai sarvāṇi bhūtāny ayācamānāyaiva baliṃ haranti ya evaṃ veda
children.translated_text: In just this way all beings bring tribute to him without being asked, whoever knows thus.
Its secret teaching is: one should not beg.

children.text: tad yathā grāmaṃ bhikṣitvā 'labdhvopaviśen nāham ato dattam aśnīyām iti
children.translated_text: It is as when, after begging in a village and receiving nothing, one sits down saying, “I will not eat what is given from here.”

children.text: ya evainaṃ purastāt pratyācakṣīraṃsta evainam upamantrayante dadāma ta iti
children.translated_text: Those very people who refused him before then invite him, saying, “Let us give to you.”
This is the rule for one who does not ask.

children.text: annadās tv evainam upamantrayante dadāma ta iti ||
children.translated_text: The food-givers themselves invite him, saying, “Let us give to you.”
<s>Prāṇa</s> is Brahman, so <s>Paiṅgya</s> used to say.

children.text: tasya vā etasya brahmaṇo vākparastāc cakṣur ārunddhe
children.translated_text: For this Brahman, speech blocks off the eye behind it.
The eye blocks off the ear behind it.
The ear blocks off the mind behind it.
The mind blocks off <s>prāṇa</s> behind it.

children.text: tasmai vā etasmai prāṇāya brahmaṇa etāḥ sarvā devatā ayācamānāyaiva baliṃ haranti
children.translated_text: To this <s>prāṇa</s>, this Brahman, all these deities bring tribute unasked.

children.text: evaṃ haivāsmai sarvāṇi bhūtāny ayācamānāyaiva baliṃ haranti ya evaṃ veda
children.translated_text: In just this way all beings bring tribute to him without being asked, whoever knows thus.
Its secret teaching is: one should not beg.

children.text: tad yathā grāmaṃ bhikṣitvā 'labhdvopaviśen nāham ato dattam aśnīyām iti
children.translated_text: It is as when, after begging in a village and receiving nothing, one sits down saying, “I will not eat what is given from here.”

children.text: ya evainaṃ purastāt pratyācakṣīraṃsta evainam upamantrayante dadāma ta iti
children.translated_text: Those very people who refused him before then invite him, saying, “Let us give to you.”
This is the rule for one who does not ask.

children.text: annadās tv evainam upamantrayante dadāma ta iti ||
children.translated_text: The food-givers themselves invite him, saying, “Let us give to you.”
Now then, the securing of a single possession.

children.text: yad ekadhanam abhidhyāyāt paurṇamāsyāṃ vāmāvāsyāṃ vā śuddhapakṣe vā puṇye nakṣatre 'gnim upasamādhāya parisamūhya paristīrya paryukṣya utpūya dakṣiṇaṃ jānv ācya sruveṇa vā camasena vā kaṃsena vaitā ājyāhutīr juhoti
children.translated_text: If one should desire a single possession, on the full moon or on the new moon, or in the bright fortnight, or under an auspicious constellation, he should set down the fire, sweep around it, strew the sacred grass, sprinkle around, purify, bend the right knee, and with a ladle, cup, or bronze vessel offer these ghee oblations.

children.text: vāṅ nāma devatāvarodhanī sā me 'muṣmād idam avarundhyāt tasyai svāhā
children.translated_text: “Speech by name is the securing deity; may she secure this for me from that person. To her, svāhā.”

children.text: prāṇo nāma devatāvarodhanī sā me 'muṣmād idam avarundhyāt tasyai svāhā
children.translated_text: “<s>Prāṇa</s> by name is the securing deity; may he secure this for me from that person. To him, svāhā.”

children.text: cakṣur nāma devatāvarodhanī sā me 'muṣmād idam avarundhyāt tasyai svāhā
children.translated_text: “The eye by name is the securing deity; may it secure this for me from that person. To it, svāhā.”

children.text: śrotraṃ nāma devatāvarodhanī sā me 'muṣmād idam avarundhyāt tasyai svāhā
children.translated_text: “The ear by name is the securing deity; may it secure this for me from that person. To it, svāhā.”

children.text: mano nāma devatāvarodhanī sā me 'muṣmād idam avarundhyāt tasyai svāhā
children.translated_text: “The mind by name is the securing deity; may it secure this for me from that person. To it, svāhā.”

children.text: prajñā nāma devatāvarodhanī sā me 'muṣmād idam avarundhyāt tasyai svāhā
children.translated_text: “Intelligence by name is the securing deity; may she secure this for me from that person. To her, svāhā.”

children.text: ity atha dhūmagandhaṃ prajighrāyājyalepenāṅgāny anuvimṛjya vācaṃyamo 'bhipravrajyārthaṃ brūyād dūtaṃ vā prahiṇuyāt
children.translated_text: Then, after smelling the scent of the smoke and rubbing his limbs with a smear of ghee, observing silence, he should go forth toward the objective and speak, or send a messenger.
He indeed obtains it.
Now then, the divine remembrance.

children.text: yasya priyo bubhūṣed yasyai vā yeṣāṃ vā yāsāṃ vaiteṣām evaikasmin parvaṇy agnim upasamādhāyaitayaivāvṛtaitā ājyāhutīr juhoti
children.translated_text: For whichever man or woman, or whichever men or women, one wishes to become dear, on one of these same lunar days he should set down the fire and, by this same procedure, offer these ghee oblations.

children.text: vācam te mayi juhomy asau svāhā
children.translated_text: “I offer your speech into myself, O so-and-so; svāhā.”

children.text: prāṇaṃ te mayi juhomy asau svāhā
children.translated_text: “I offer your <s>prāṇa</s> into myself, O so-and-so; svāhā.”

children.text: cakṣus te mayi juhomy asau svāhā
children.translated_text: “I offer your eye into myself, O so-and-so; svāhā.”

children.text: śrotraṃ te mayi juhomy asau svāhā
children.translated_text: “I offer your ear into myself, O so-and-so; svāhā.”

children.text: manas te mayi juhomy asau svāhā
children.translated_text: “I offer your mind into myself, O so-and-so; svāhā.”

children.text: prajñāṃ te mayi juhomy asau svāhā
children.translated_text: “I offer your intelligence into myself, O so-and-so; svāhā.”

children.text: ityatha dhūmagandhaṃ prajighrāyājyalepenāṅgāny anuvimṛjya vacaṃyamo 'bhipravrajya saṃsparśaṃ jigamiṣet
children.translated_text: Then, after smelling the scent of the smoke and rubbing his limbs with a smear of ghee, observing silence, he should go forth and seek bodily contact.
Or he should stand speaking even from upwind.
He indeed becomes dear, and they indeed remember him.

children.text: athātaḥ saṃyamanaṃ prātardanam āntaram agnihotram iti cācakṣate
children.translated_text: Now then, the restraint, the <s>Prātardana</s>, which they call the inner agnihotra.

children.text: yāvad vai puruṣo bhāṣate na tāvat prāṇituṃ śaknoti
children.translated_text: For as long as a person speaks, he is not able to breathe.
At that time he offers breath into speech.

children.text: yāvad vai puruṣaḥ prāṇiti na tāvad bhāṣituṃ śaknoti
children.translated_text: For as long as a person breathes, he is not able to speak.
At that time he offers speech into breath.

children.text: ete anante amṛte āhutī jāgrac ca svapaṃś ca santataṃ avyavacchinnaṃ juhoti
children.translated_text: Waking and sleeping, he continually offers these two endless, immortal oblations without interruption.

children.text: atha yā anyā āhutayo 'ntavatyas tāḥ karmamayyo hi bhavanti
children.translated_text: But the other oblations are finite, for they are made of ritual action.

children.text: etad dha vai pūrve vidvāṃso 'gnihotraṃ na juhavāñ cakruḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the ancient knowers did not perform the agnihotra as an external offering.
<s>Śuṣkabhṛṅgāra</s> used to say, "The uktha is brahman."
One should worship it as the Ṛg.
All beings worship him for preeminence.
One should worship it as the Yajus.
All beings are joined to him for preeminence.
One should worship it as the Sāman.
All beings bow down to him for preeminence.
One should worship it as splendor.
One should worship it as fame.
One should worship it as brilliance.

children.text: tad yathaitac chastrāṇāṃ śrīmattamaṃ yaśasvitamaṃ tejasvitamaṃ bhavati tatho evaivaṃ vidvān sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ śrīmattamo yaśasvitamas tejasvitamo bhavati
children.translated_text: Just as this is the most splendid, the most famous, and the most brilliant of the recitations, so one who knows thus becomes the most splendid, the most famous, and the most brilliant of all beings.

children.text: tad etad aiṣṭikaṃ karmamayam ātmānam adhvaryuḥ saṃskaroti
children.translated_text: The adhvaryu prepares this self, made of ritual action, belonging to the iṣṭi.
Into it he weaves what consists of Yajus.
Into what consists of Yajus the hotṛ weaves what consists of Ṛg.
Into what consists of Ṛg the udgātṛ weaves what consists of Sāman.
This is the self of the threefold knowledge.

children.text: eṣa u evaitad indrasyātmā bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: This indeed becomes the self of <s>Indra</s> for one who knows thus.

children.text: athātaḥ sarvajitaḥ kauṣītakes trīṇy upāsanāni bhavanti
children.translated_text: Now, then, there are three meditations of <s>Sarvajit Kauṣītaki</s>.

children.text: sarvajid dha sma kauṣītakir udyantam ādityam upatiṣṭhate yajñopavītaṃ kṛtvodakam ānīya triḥ prasicyodapātraṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Sarvajit Kauṣītaki</s> used to stand near the rising sun, having put on the sacred thread, brought water, and sprinkled the water-vessel three times.
He would say, "You are the remover; remove my evil."

children.text: etayaivāvṛtā madhye santam udvargo 'si pāpmānaṃ ma udvṛṅdhīti
children.translated_text: In this same manner, when it is in the middle, he would say, "You are the up-remover; remove up my evil."

children.text: etayaivāvṛtāstaṃ yantaṃ saṃvargo 'si pāpmānaṃ me saṃvṛṅdhīti
children.translated_text: In this same manner, when it is setting, he would say, "You are the gatherer; gather away my evil."

children.text: tad yad ahorātrābhyāṃ pāpam akarot saṃ sma tad vṛṅkte
children.translated_text: Whatever evil he had done by day or night, he thus gathered away.
In just this way one who knows should stand near the sun with this same procedure.

children.text: yad ahorātrābhyāṃ pāpaṃ karoti saṃ tad vṛṅkte ||
children.translated_text: Whatever evil he does by day or night, he gathers it away.

children.text: atha māsi māsy amāvāsyāyāṃ paścāc candramasaṃ dṛśyamānam upatiṣṭhetaitayaivāvṛtā haritatṛṇe vā pratyasyati
children.translated_text: Then, month by month, on the new-moon day, he should stand near the moon when it is visible in the west, with this same procedure, or he casts away green grass.

children.text: yan me susamid dhṛdayam adhi candramasi śritaṃ
children.translated_text: "That well-kindled heart of mine which rests upon the moon,

children.text: manye 'haṃ māṃ tad vidvāṃsaṃ māhaṃ putryam aghaṃ rudam
children.translated_text: I think of that as knowing me; may I not weep over misfortune concerning a son."

children.text: iti na hy asmāt pūrvā prajāḥ praitīti
children.translated_text: So he says, for offspring born before him do not pass away from him.
Then, looking closely, he should touch his wife's heart.

children.text: yat te suśīme hṛdayaṃ śritam antaḥ prajāpatau
children.translated_text: "That heart of yours, O fair one, which rests within <s>Prajāpati</s>,

children.text: tenāmṛtatvasyeśāne mā tvaṃ putryam aghaṃ nigāḥ
children.translated_text: by that, O mistress of immortality, may you not fall into misfortune concerning a son."

children.text: iti na hy asyāḥ pūrvā prajāḥ praitīti
children.translated_text: So he says, for offspring born before her do not pass away from her.
Thus for one whose son has been born.
Now for one whose son has not been born:
"Swell up; may it come together for you.

children.text: saṃ te payāṃsi sam u yantu vājāḥ
children.translated_text: May your milks come together, and may your strengths come together.
The ray which the <s>Ādityas</s> cause to swell,
so it is."

children.text: etās tisra ṛco japitvā māsmākaṃ prāṇena prajayā paśubhir āpyāyiṣṭhāḥ
children.translated_text: Having murmured these three verses, he says, "Do not swell at the expense of our breath, offspring, and cattle.

children.text: yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣmas tasya prāṇena prajayā paśubhir āpyāyasveti
children.translated_text: Whoever hates us, and whomever we hate, swell at the expense of his breath, offspring, and cattle."
"I turn with the <s>Aindra</s> course.
I follow the course of the sun."
So saying, he turns his right arm around.

children.text: atha paurṇamāsyāṃ purastāc candramasaṃ dṛśyamānam upatiṣṭhetaitayaivāvṛtā
children.translated_text: Then, on the full-moon day, he should stand near the moon when it is visible in the east, with this same procedure.
"You are king <s>Soma</s>, clear-sighted.
You are five-mouthed <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: brāhmaṇas ta ekaṃ mukhaṃ tena mukhena rājño 'tsi
children.translated_text: One mouth of yours is the brahmin; with that mouth you eat kings.
With that mouth make me an eater of food.

children.text: rājā ta ekaṃ mukhaṃ tena mukhena viśo 'tsi
children.translated_text: One mouth of yours is the king; with that mouth you eat the clansmen.
With that mouth make me an eater of food.

children.text: śyenas ta ekaṃ mukhaṃ tena mukhena pakṣiṇo 'tsi
children.translated_text: One mouth of yours is the falcon; with that mouth you eat the birds.
With that mouth make me an eater of food.

children.text: agniṣ ṭa ekaṃ mukhaṃ tena mukhenemaṃ lokam atsi
children.translated_text: One mouth of yours is fire; with that mouth you eat this world.
With that mouth make me an eater of food.

children.text: tvayi pañcamaṃ mukhaṃ tena mukhena sarvāṇi bhūtāny atsi
children.translated_text: In you is the fifth mouth; with that mouth you eat all beings.
With that mouth make me an eater of food.
Do not wane away through our breath, offspring, and cattle.

children.text: yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣmas tasya prāṇena prajayā paśubhir apakṣīyasva
children.translated_text: Whoever hates us, and whomever we hate, wane away through his breath, offspring, and cattle."
"I turn with the divine course.
I follow the course of the sun."
So saying, he turns his right arm around.
Then, when he has returned from a journey, he should smell the head of his son.
"From limb after limb you have arisen; from the heart you are born.

children.text: ātmā tvaṃ putra māvitha sa jīva śaradaḥ śatam
children.translated_text: You are my self, son; do not harm me. Live a hundred autumns.
So-and-so,"
so he takes his name.

children.text: aśmā bhava paraśur bhava hiraṇyam astṛtaṃ bhava
children.translated_text: "Be a stone; be an axe; be unassailable gold.

children.text: tejo vai putra nāmāsi sa jīva śaradaḥ śatam
children.translated_text: For brilliance, son, is your name. Live a hundred autumns.
So-and-so,"
so he takes his name.
Then he embraces him.
"With that by which <s>Prajāpati</s> embraced creatures for their safety,
with that I embrace you.
So-and-so,"
so he takes his name.
Then he murmurs into his right ear:
"Grant to this one, O bountiful <s>Maghavan</s>, O strong one,"
so he says.
"O <s>Indra</s>, bestow the best treasures,"
so he says into the left ear.

children.text: mā chitthā mā vyathiṣṭhāḥ śataṃ śarada āyuṣaḥ
children.translated_text: "Do not be cut off; do not be shaken. May you have a hundred autumns of life.

children.text: jīvasva putra te nāmnā mūrdhānam abhijighrāmi
children.translated_text: Live, son. By your name I smell your head.
So-and-so."
Thus he should smell the head three times.

children.text: gavām tvā hiṅkāreṇābhihiṅkaromīti trir mūrdhānam abhihiṅkuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Saying, "I bellow over you with the bellowing of the cows," he should bellow over the head three times.
Now then, the divine passing-away.

children.text: etad vai brahma dīpyate yad agnir jvalaty athaitan mriyate yan na jvalati
children.translated_text: This indeed is <s>brahman</s> shining: when fire blazes. And this dies when it does not blaze.

children.text: tasyādityam eva tejo gacchati vāyuṃ prāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Its radiance goes to the sun, its breath to the wind.

children.text: etad vai brahma dīpyate yad ādityo dṛśyate 'thaitan mriyate yan na dṛśyate
children.translated_text: This indeed is <s>brahman</s> shining: when the sun is seen. And this dies when it is not seen.

children.text: tasya candramasam eva tejo gacchati vāyuṃ prāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Its radiance goes to the moon, its breath to the wind.

children.text: etad vai brahma dīpyate yac candramā dṛśyate 'thaitan mriyate yan na dṛśyate
children.translated_text: This indeed is <s>brahman</s> shining: when the moon is seen. And this dies when it is not seen.

children.text: tasya vidyutam eva tejo gacchati vāyuṃ prāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Its radiance goes to lightning, its breath to the wind.

children.text: etad vai brahma dīpyate yad vidyud vidyotate 'thaitan mriyate yan na vidyotate
children.translated_text: This indeed is <s>brahman</s> shining: when lightning flashes. And this dies when it does not flash.

children.text: tasya vāyum eva tejo gacchati vāyuṃ prāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Its radiance goes to the wind, its breath to the wind.

children.text: tā vā etāḥ sarvā devatā vāyum eva praviśya vāyau mṛtvā na mūrchante
children.translated_text: All these deities, having entered the wind and died in the wind, do not become unconscious.
From that very source they rise again.
Thus with reference to the deities.
Now with reference to the self.

children.text: etad vai brahma dīpyate yad vācā vadaty athaitan mriyate yan na vadati
children.translated_text: This indeed is <s>brahman</s> shining: when one speaks with speech. And this dies when one does not speak.

children.text: tasya cakṣur eva tejo gacchati prāṇaṃ prāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Its radiance goes to the eye, its breath to <s>prāṇa</s> (breath).

children.text: etad vai brahma dīpyate yac cakṣuṣā paśyaty athaitan mriyate yan na paśyati
children.translated_text: This indeed is <s>brahman</s> shining: when one sees with the eye. And this dies when one does not see.

children.text: tasya śrotram eva tejo gacchati prāṇaṃ prāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Its radiance goes to hearing, its breath to <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: etad vai brahma dīpyate yac chrotreṇa śṛṇoty athaitan mriyate yan na śṛṇoti
children.translated_text: This indeed is <s>brahman</s> shining: when one hears with hearing. And this dies when one does not hear.

children.text: tasya mana eva tejo gacchati prāṇaṃ prāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Its radiance goes to the mind, its breath to <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: etad vai brahma dīpyate yan manasā dhyāyaty athaitan mriyate yan na dhyāyati
children.translated_text: This indeed is <s>brahman</s> shining: when one thinks with the mind. And this dies when one does not think.

children.text: tasya prāṇam eva tejo gacchati prāṇaṃ prāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Its radiance goes to <s>prāṇa</s>, its breath to <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: tā vā etāḥ sarvā devatāḥ prāṇam eva praviśya prāṇe mṛtvā na mūrchante
children.translated_text: All these deities, having entered <s>prāṇa</s> and died in <s>prāṇa</s>, do not become unconscious.
From that very source they rise again.

children.text: tad yadi ha vā evaṃ vidvāṃsam ubhau parvatāv abhipravarteyātāṃ dakṣinaś cottaraś ca tustūrṣamānau na hainaṃ stṛṇvīyātām
children.translated_text: If, indeed, the southern and northern mountains were to roll upon one who knows this in this way, desiring to crush him, they would not crush him.

children.text: atha ya enaṃ dviṣanti yāṃś ca svayaṃ dveṣṭi ta evainaṃ parimriyante ||
children.translated_text: But those who hate him, and those whom he himself hates, they alone perish around him.
Now then, the taking of the supreme good.

children.text: etā ha vai devatā ahaṃśreyase vivadamānā asmāc charīrād uccakramuḥ
children.translated_text: These deities, disputing over preeminence, went out from this body.
Then it lay there without breathing, dried up, become like wood.
Then speech entered it.
It spoke with speech, but still lay there.
Then sight entered it.

children.text: tad vācā vadac cakṣuṣā paśyac chiṣya eva
children.translated_text: It spoke with speech and saw with sight, but still lay there.
Then hearing entered it.

children.text: tad vācā vadac cakṣuṣā paśyac chrotreṇa śṛṇvac chiṣya eva
children.translated_text: It spoke with speech, saw with sight, and heard with hearing, but still lay there.
Then mind entered it.

children.text: tad vācā vadac cakṣuṣā paśyac chrotreṇa śṛṇvan manasā dhyāyac chiṣya eva
children.translated_text: It spoke with speech, saw with sight, heard with hearing, and thought with mind, but still lay there.
Then <s>prāṇa</s> entered it.
At once it rose up from that state.

children.text: tā vā etāḥ sarvā devatāḥ prāṇe niḥśreyasaṃ viditvā prāṇam eva prajñātmānam abhisambhūya sahaivaite sarve 'smāccharīrād uccakramuḥ
children.translated_text: All these deities, having recognized the supreme good in <s>prāṇa</s>, and having become one with <s>prāṇa</s>, the self of intelligence, went out from this body together with him.
Having entered the wind, with space as their self, they went to heaven.

children.text: tatho evaivaṃ vidvān prāṇe niḥśreyasaṃ viditvā sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ prāṇam eva prajñātmānam abhisambhūya sahaivaitaiḥ sarvair asmāc charīrād utkrāmati
children.translated_text: So too one who knows this, having recognized the supreme good in <s>prāṇa</s>, and having become one with <s>prāṇa</s>, the self of intelligence of all beings, departs from this body together with all these.
Having entered the wind, with space as his self, he goes to heaven.
He goes there where these gods are.

children.text: tat prāpya yad amṛtā devās tad amṛto bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Having reached that, because the gods are immortal, he becomes immortal who knows this.
Now then, what they call the father-to-son transmission.

children.text: pitā putraṃ preṣyann āhvayati navais tṛṇair agāraṃ saṃstīryāgnim upasamādhāyodakumbhaṃ sapātram upanidhāyāhatena vāsasā sampracchannaḥ pitā śete
children.translated_text: When the father is about to depart, he calls his son; having strewn the house with fresh grasses, having kindled the fire, and having placed nearby a water pot with a vessel, the father lies down covered with an unworn garment.

children.text: etya putra upariṣṭād abhinipadyata indriyair indriyāṇi saṃspṛśya
children.translated_text: The son comes and lies down upon him from above, touching organs with organs.
Or else he may transmit it to him while he is seated facing him.
Then he hands it over to him.
The father says, "I place my speech in you."

children.text: vācaṃ te mayi dadha iti putraḥ
children.translated_text: The son says, "Place your speech in me."
The father says, "I place my breath in you."

children.text: prāṇaṃ te mayi dadha iti putraḥ
children.translated_text: The son says, "Place your breath in me."
The father says, "I place my sight in you."

children.text: cakṣus te mayi dadha iti putraḥ
children.translated_text: The son says, "Place your sight in me."
The father says, "I place my hearing in you."

children.text: śrotraṃ te mayi dadha iti putraḥ
children.translated_text: The son says, "Place your hearing in me."
The father says, "I place my food-essences in you."

children.text: annarasāṃs te mayi dadha iti putraḥ
children.translated_text: The son says, "Place your food-essences in me."
The father says, "I place my actions in you."

children.text: karmāṇi te mayi dadha iti putraḥ
children.translated_text: The son says, "Place your actions in me."
The father says, "I place my pleasure and pain in you."

children.text: sukhaduḥkhe te mayi dadha iti putraḥ
children.translated_text: The son says, "Place your pleasure and pain in me."

children.text: ānandaṃ ratiṃ prajātiṃ me tvayi dadhānīti pitā
children.translated_text: The father says, "I place my bliss, delight, and procreation in you."

children.text: ānandaṃ ratiṃ prajātiṃ te mayi dadha iti putraḥ
children.translated_text: The son says, "Place your bliss, delight, and procreation in me."
The father says, "I place my goings in you."

children.text: ityās te mayi dadha iti putraḥ
children.translated_text: The son says, "Place your goings in me."
The father says, "I place my mind in you."

children.text: manas te mayi dadha iti putraḥ
children.translated_text: The son says, "Place your mind in me."
The father says, "I place my understanding in you."

children.text: prajñāṃ te mayi dadha iti putraḥ
children.translated_text: The son says, "Place your understanding in me."

children.text: yady u vā upābhigadaḥ syāt samāsenaiva brūyāt prāṇān me tvayi dadhānīti pitā
children.translated_text: But if he is unable to speak much, the father should say summarily, "I place my vital breaths in you."

children.text: prāṇāṃs te mayi dadha iti putraḥ
children.translated_text: The son says, "Place your breaths in me."
Then, turning to the right, he goes out toward the east.

children.text: taṃ pitānumantrayate yaśo brahmavarcasaṃ kīrtis tvā juṣatām iti
children.translated_text: The father addresses him with a mantra: "May fame, brahmanic splendor, and renown favor you."

children.text: athetaraḥ savyam anv aṃsam abhyavekṣate pāṇināntardhāya vasanāntena vā pracchādya svargān lokān kāmān āpnuhīti
children.translated_text: Then the other looks over his left shoulder, either concealing it with his hand or covering it with the end of his garment, and says, "May you obtain the heavenly worlds and desired objects."

children.text: sa yady agadaḥ syāt putrasyaiśvarye pitā vaset pari vā vrajet
children.translated_text: If he should be free from illness, the father should live under the son's authority, or he may go wandering.

children.text: yady u vai preyāt tathaivainaṃ samāpayeyur yathā samāpayitavyo bhavati yathā samāpayitavyo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: But if he should die, then they should complete the rites for him just as one who is to be completed should be completed, just as one who is to be completed should be completed.
